extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and USPTO officials involved in disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for an affidavit of resignation consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, including required acknowledgements, publication obligations, and reinstatement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent / no coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that the practitioner's consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and that the practitioner is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit plain-language statement in the affidavit that consent is voluntary; this is a threshold for approving exclusion on consent under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of OED investigation and factual basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must acknowledge awareness that the OED Director opened an investigation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22 and that the investigation obtained information about the practitioner's conduct (e.g., federal criminal conviction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should identify the investigation and the relevant factual matters (the Final Order cites the practitioner's October 19, 2017 guilty plea and sentencing on money laundering charges, including case citation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of OED opinion of rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit should acknowledge that the OED Director is of the opinion, based on the investigation, that the practitioner violated specified provisions of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists specific rule provisions (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b), (c), and/or (i)) that the OED believed were violated; the affidavit should reference the OED's opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11.804(b) — criminal act reflecting adversely on fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a practitioner in other respects (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the OED opinion alleges this subsection, the affidavit should acknowledge awareness of that allegation; the Rule provides the substantive basis for discipline when criminal conduct impacts professional fitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11.804(c) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit may acknowledge that the OED opined the practitioner's conduct implicated this subsection; this subsection is a ground for discipline independent of a criminal conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11.804(i) — other conduct reflecting adversely on fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This residual provision covers conduct not explicitly listed elsewhere; the affidavit may acknowledge allegations under this subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumptions (conclusive presumptions by OED Director)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that, if and when the practitioner applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for purposes of determining reinstatement that (a) the facts in the investigation are true, and (b) the practitioner could not have successfully defended against the allegations embodied in the OED Director's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should contain plain acknowledgment of both subparts (a) and (b); this limits the practitioner's ability to relitigate factual findings during a reinstatement application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with and acknowledgment of relevant regulations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the practitioner has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should identify the listed sections and explicitly acknowledge understanding of their consequences (e.g., effect of exclusion, reinstatement procedures, and obligations while excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit consent to exclusion from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must expressly consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear statement of consent in the affidavit is required for exclusion on consent to be approved and effective as the Final Order directs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory authority to approve resignation and exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has authority, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits and orders are processed under those statutory/regulatory authorities; practitioners and counsel should reference these authorities when filing or evaluating resignation affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of affidavit required for exclusion to take effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director must determine the affidavit of resignation complies with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) and approve it; upon approval the practitioner's exclusion on consent commences as ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states that, based on compliance, the affidavit is approved and exclusion commences on the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires public posting of disciplinary decisions involving practitioners; include the provided URL for access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice requirement and content consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided sample notice concerning the practitioner's exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order supplies model notice language describing the exclusion, the basis (e.g., conviction), the alleged rule violations, and the effect on future reinstatement considerations; Official Gazette publication should track that language materially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties while excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 governs duties of excluded practitioners (e.g., notice to clients, withdrawal, handling of files); the Final Order expressly requires compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 (reinstatement procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.60 sets standards and procedures for seeking reinstatement; the affidavit must acknowledge the reinstatement presumptions and the practitioner must follow § 11.60 when applying.
